subject: Embedded ISV account entanglement — carve/stitch proposal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Sara Morales <sara@orbisanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Embedded ISV account entanglement — carve/stitch proposal

Team / Sara,

Quick summary: EdgeBeam (customer) has multiple active opportunities where an embedded ISV partner (Embedded, Inc.) is both the systems integrator and a product reseller inside the same named accounts. The partner has relationship ties with two separate Redwood sales motions — a direct field AE and a channel ISV lead — which has led to duplicate pipeline entries and confusion over who should own renewal conversations.

I attached our working account map (edgebeam-partner-map.xlsx) and an early stitch proposal (stitch-plan-v1.md). High-level ask: can we agree to a short-term carve + stitching approach that lets the field AE retain commercial ownership for a set of top 20 accounts while establishing a lightweight ambassador model for Embedded, Inc. to continue integration/reselling in the remaining footprint? This needs to be quick and low-friction for the customer.

Key constraints:
- Customer prefers a single point of contact for contract/renewal conversations.
- Embedded, Inc. will not accept a full territory handback; they want a delegated technical reseller role.
- We need to avoid duplicate opportunities in CRM as of EOW next Friday.

Requested next steps:
1) Marissa — propose canonical carve list and which accounts the field AE should keep.
2) Karthik — quick technical gating: can we support ambassador-based SKUs and routing?
3) Sara/TJ — confirm customer preference and whether Embedded, Inc. is amenable to the ambassador model.

Thanks — attaching both files for reference.

Attachments: [edgebeam-partner-map.xlsx (xlsx)], [stitch-plan-v1.md (md)]

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0112

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Morales <sara@orbisanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-10-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embedded ISV account entanglement — carve/stitch proposal

Jonas — thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed the map and created a proposed carve: a top-20 list where the field AE is the commercial owner and we mark Embedded, Inc. as the technical ambassador (no commercial co-ownership). For the remaining accounts, Embedded, Inc. keeps co-sell privileges.

A few notes:
- The carve preserves existing renewals through Q1 '28 and avoids reassigning any live RFPs.
- I added a short decision matrix to the stitch-plan that maps signals (ARR, renewal date, expansion stage) to carve vs. co-sell.

If everyone is OK, I can convert the carve list into HubSpot ownership updates and a one-line partner-facing AM email for the customer.

Marissa
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-10-30T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embedded ISV account entanglement — carve/stitch proposal

Quick technical readout from infra/integrations: ambassador model is feasible with two caveats
1) We need to create a partner-scoped API key (read-only usage + telemetry) if Embedded, Inc. requires access to dev/test instances — this avoids cross-account data bleed.
2) For billing/commerce we need a single invoice flow; if Embedded, Inc. invoices separately we must route charges through our reseller tokens (we have a fast path, but finance needs 7–10 business days to set it up).

Operational ask: if we proceed, please let me know the final carve list and indicate which accounts require a time-limited reseller token (I can pre-stage them).

Also: the stitch-plan includes a short automated CRM dedupe rule (by customer site + product SKU) — I can drop this into HubSpot as a workflow.

Karthik
Director, Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

> On Oct 29, 2027, Marissa Cole wrote:
> > proposed carve attached

From: Sara Morales <sara@orbisanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: TJ Chen <tj@embedded.isv>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embedded ISV account entanglement — carve/stitch proposal

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the clear proposal. EdgeBeam's procurement and GTM teams prefer a single commercial owner per account for negotiations — that matches Jonas' note. They are comfortable with Embedded, Inc. acting as an ambassador/reseller for non-top-20 accounts provided that: 1) Redwood is the contracting party for the top-20 carve; and 2) Embedded, Inc. has a documented delegated reseller scope and a technical access agreement.

Attached is a short list of accounts that the customer specifically flagged as must-stay-with-field (6 accounts) and a handy contact list for each account owner. If we implement the ambassador model the customer asks that communications to the executive sponsor be routed from Redwood (not Embedded, Inc.).

Sara Morales
Strategic Customer Success, Orbis Analytics (EdgeBeam SI)
sara@orbisanalytics.com

Attachment: [edgebeam-customer-priority-list.csv (csv)]

Thanks all — good alignment. Action items and owners below:

1) Marissa: finalize HubSpot owner updates for the top-20 carve (target: 2027-11-05) and share the partner-facing notification email copy (I will review).
2) Karthik: stage partner-scoped API tokens and the CRM dedupe workflow (target: 2027-11-09).
3) Lauren: coordinate finance + contracts for delegated reseller token and confirm timeline for invoicing flow (cc finance@redwood.ai).

I'll draft a short executive note to EdgeBeam confirming single-point commercial ownership and the ambassador technical model. We'll include the attachments and the HubSpot change log.
